reviews.reasoning: Span and seam affirmed. Ps 81 is shift+1: web:Ps.81.1-5 = oshb:Ps.81.2-6, and the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.81.0 = oshb:Ps.81.1 is correct (mt_title_verses ['Ps.81.1']) and owner-ruled admissible on an opening row. Every Hebrew run in the row re-collates at byte tier against its cited ref (collate.py, 7 runs). The close at web:Ps.81.5|81.6 = oshb:Ps.81.6|81.7 is well warranted from the bytes: oshb:Ps.81.6 ends on the unmarked 1cs אֶשְׁמָֽע while oshb:Ps.81.7 opens the oracle on the 1cs perfect הֲסִיר֣וֹתִי, so the ambiguity the row rests on is real and the seam sits where the ambiguity resolves. Three defects, none of which move the seam: a device-membership count contradicted by the inventory and by a byte sweep; a pair of curly-quoted WEB imperatives attached to a Hebrew form that renders neither; a gloss that drops the very token the seam argument depends on; and a positional row reference.

challenges.claim: device_notes states that Psalm 81 shares the al-haggittit label with Psalm 8 alone ('2 of 150 psalms'); the label stands in three psalm titles, so the figure is false.

The byte sweep returns only 1 verse because the accent differs in each title, which is why the count must be taken at skeleton tier and the tier named. psalm_device_inventory.json genre_label_membership.al_haggittit = [8, 81, 84]. The row's digit understates by one psalm; the correct claim is 3 psalms (skeleton tier, verse unit), Ps 84 being the omitted member.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] binds two curly-quoted WEB imperatives to a quoted Hebrew form that renders neither, and omits the second imperative actually standing in the cited verse.
challenges.evidence: The field quotes הַ֭רְנִינוּ at oshb:Ps.81.2 and then supplies 'raise' web:Ps.81.2 and 'blow' web:Ps.81.3. WEB renders that form at web:Ps.81.1 = oshb:Ps.81.2 as “Sing aloud to God, our strength!”. “Raise a song, and bring here the tambourine, the pleasant lyre with the harp.” at web:Ps.81.2 renders שְֽׂאוּ of oshb:Ps.81.3, and “Blow the trumpet at the New Moon,” at web:Ps.81.3 renders תִּקְע֣וּ of oshb:Ps.81.4 — two different verses, each shift+1. The form that actually makes 'imperatives' plural inside oshb:Ps.81.2, הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ, is not cited at all. Both English words are byte-verbatim WEB at the refs given, so the defect is the binding, not the quoting.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span mismatch at oshb:Ps.81.6: the four-token Hebrew quote is glossed by a WEB clause that drops its verb — the one token the row's voice-ambiguity argument rests on.
challenges.evidence: Quoted: שְׂפַ֖ת לֹא יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶשְׁמָֽע (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.81.6, 4 tokens). Gloss supplied: 'a language that I didn't know'. The witness reads “I heard a language that I didn’t know.” at web:Ps.81.5 = oshb:Ps.81.6; the gloss is that clause minus its verb, so the quoted אֶשְׁמָֽע is unglossed. The row argues that this clause 'sits grammatically ambiguous between the psalmist's and the divine voice' — an argument carried entirely by that 1cs form. Quote/gloss parity requires the gloss to be re-cut to the quoted span rather than truncated.

Distinct from the row's use of 'row-external' in observed_substrate_signals[2], which refers to the row's own span boundary rather than to another row's position and is legitimate disclosure.

The selah handling is exemplary and I affirm it: pmarks_Ps.json carries exactly 1 selah entry in Ps 81, oshb:Ps.81.8 = web:Ps.81.7 (1 verse, 1 occurrence), it falls inside this row's own span, and the row explicitly demotes it to corroboration — span-scoped symmetry intact, no absence claim made outside the span. The row-external citations (the oracle-onset form at oshb:Ps.81.7, the adversative at oshb:Ps.81.12) are disclosed as row-external and mirrored in the refs array. challenges.claim: rejected_alternative frames the web:Ps.81.7|81.8 rival as resting on the selah and dismisses it with the assertion that web:Ps.81.8-10 continues 'without a renewed discourse marker'; oshb:Ps.81.9 (= web:Ps.81.8) opens on an imperative plus double vocative, so the rival carries an independent tier-1 driver and the stated ground is contradicted by the bytes.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.81.9 opens שְׁמַ֣ע עַ֭מִּי וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.81.9; dual-cite web:Ps.81.8 = oshb:Ps.81.9, shift+1): imperative שְׁמַ֣ע + vocative עַ֭מִּי + vocative יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל. Vocative openings and imperative clusters are named tier-1 internal-seam signals in the book's own row-granularity policy, so the rival at this seam does not rest on the selah the row attributes it to. The witness corroborates: web:Ps.81.7 closes its speech block after “I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” and web:Ps.81.8 opens a fresh one, “Hear, my people, and I will testify to you, Israel, if you would listen to me!”. A replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original; here the stated ground — an absence of renewed marking — is falsified by the first verse it covers, and the rival is credited only to a tier-3 corroborator it does not need. The row's own span is unaffected: I do not contest 81.6-81.10, which the self-identification close at oshb:Ps.81.11 supports. The rival disclosure needs re-authoring on a ground the bytes support.

challenges.claim: Two curly-quoted strings in observed_substrate_signals are model glosses, not WEB text, and neither field carries an inline web: ref.

The witness reads “I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” with the speech-close mark standing between it and Selah. at web:Ps.81.7, and “But my people didn’t listen to my voice.” at web:Ps.81.11. Both strings gloss Hebrew — עַל מֵ֖י at oshb:Ps.81.8 and וְלֹא at oshb:Ps.81.12 (byte tier) — so curly quotes misattribute them to the witness; curly quotes are reserved for WEB text and the in-field web: ref is mandatory at every layer. check_web_quotes.py flags both fields (2 of the 9 flags this cluster raises).

reviews.reasoning: Substance affirmed on every count I can test. Dual-cites correct (web:Ps.81.11-16 = oshb:Ps.81.12-17), both Hebrew runs re-collate at byte tier, and the span closes the psalm exactly at oshb:Ps.81.17. The rejected_alternative's grammatical core is byte-supportable: the counterfactual protasis ל֗וּ עַ֭מִּי שֹׁמֵ֣עַֽ לִ֑י (oshb:Ps.81.14 = web:Ps.81.13) answers the report וְלֹא שָׁמַ֣ע עַמִּ֣י לְקוֹלִ֑י (oshb:Ps.81.12 = web:Ps.81.11) by inverting the same three elements — the people, the verb of hearing, and the 1cs object — and its apodosis follows immediately at oshb:Ps.81.15 (כִּ֭מְעַט), so the report-plus-wish unit is one row on the bytes, not on taste. Two apparatus defects only, both low. Observation, not a challenge: 'no independent opening marker' is loose, since ל֗וּ is itself a clause-initial counterfactual particle; the row's own signal names the marker class it means ('no vocative or imperative break'), so the warrant survives.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] presents the gloss 'But... not' in curly quotes with no inline web: ref, attributing to the witness an English string it does not contain.

challenges.claim: The row's lead device claim — a 'triple negative-imperative' plea at oshb:Ps.83.2 — is contradicted by the pointed bytes in all three members: the first is not a verb at all, and the other two are prefix-conjugation forms.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.83.2 = web:Ps.83.1 reads אֱלֹהִ֥ים אַל דֳּמִי לָ֑ךְ אַל תֶּחֱרַ֖שׁ וְאַל תִּשְׁקֹ֣ט אֵֽל (byte tier). Member 1: אַל דֳּמִי לָ֑ךְ — the token דֳּמִי carries no prefix consonant and so cannot be a prefix-conjugation form; the -i ending would make it a feminine-singular imperative, which the addressee excludes, since the vocative is אֱלֹהִ֥ים and the two following verbs are masculine-singular. The clause is verbless. That token appears in 1 verse book-wide, oshb:Ps.83.2, at byte and at whole-token skeleton tier alike. Members 2-3: אַל תֶּחֱרַ֖שׁ and וְאַל תִּשְׁקֹ֣ט are t-prefix forms negated by אַל, the negation that pairs with the prefix conjugation rather than with the imperative form — jussives. The witness cannot rescue the label, since WEB levels all three: “God, don’t keep silent. Don’t keep silent, and don’t be still, God.” at web:Ps.83.1. Form claims are not machine-verifiable with the staged extract and must be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses; done that way, the bytes fail the label three times over. The claim recurs verbatim in rationale and in observed_substrate_signals[0], so the cure is one edit installed in both fields.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[1] claims 'six additional figures' for web:Ps.83.9-11 while its own parenthetical enumerates seven, and the counted object is never named.

The one reading that yields 6 — persons only, excluding Midian as a people — is itself contradicted by the parenthetical, which lists Midian among the figures. Count discipline requires the object (persons vs names vs peoples) to be named before the digit; as written no reading reconciles the digit with its own list.
